subject: Alticloud: strict inferencing controls — region pin & disable fallback?

Subject: Prod request — strict region pin + no fallback for PCI workloads

Priyom / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To recap our compliance review: AltiCloud will be migrating card-processing inference calls to Redwood. For our PCI environment we need to be absolutely certain that (1) all inference for the PCI workload stays inside our designated us-east-1 region, and (2) there is no automatic fallback to any other model variant or region if capacity is constrained.

Can Redwood support a hard region pin + disable-fallback policy scoped to a single model version for our production tenant? Our security team asks for a short write-up of how that would be enforced and what the outage/failover behavior is if capacity is exceeded.

I attached the PCI requirements doc and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Please loop in product/infra and let me know next steps.

—Alan
Alan Foster
Head of Platform Security, AltiCloud

Attachments: Alticloud_PCI_requirements_v2.pdf, alticloud-proposed-map.xlsx

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alan Foster <alan@alticloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod request — strict region pin + no fallback for PCI workloads

Thanks Alan — looping in Neha (Product) and Marcus (Infra) to scope. Short answer: we can implement a region pin and disable automatic fallback, but it has operational tradeoffs (risk of hard rejects when capacity is exhausted). We'll propose options below and outline the expected behaviors.

Plan (high level):
- Option A: Hard region lock + disable fallback (rejects when capacity exceeded). Suitable for strong compliance needs; requires reserved capacity or guaranteed Dedicated pool.
- Option B: Region lock + queued requests with SLA breach alerts (keeps requests in-flight but increases latency).
- Option C: Soft lock: prefer region/model but allow fallback after configurable timeout — lower availability risk.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm if we can provision a Dedicated pool for AC-2027-112 on a 1-month trial and the lead time? Neha, I'll need a short product note describing enforcement points (router layer, token routing, model-var mapping) for Alan's security team.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:03 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Alan — looping in Neha (Product) and Marcus (Infra) to scope. Short answer: we can implement a region pin and disable automatic fallback, but it has operational tradeoffs (risk of hard rejects when capacity is exhausted). We'll propose options below and outline the expected behaviors.

We can do Option A but it requires one of two things up front: (1) Dedicated capacity committed (monthly) sized to peak qps + buffer, or (2) a hard rate-limit that returns a 429 when capacity is reached. Implementation notes:
- Router: add a per-tenant region hard-pin flag that causes route resolution to skip cross-region candidate lists.
- Fallback: add a tenant-scoped toggle to disable the fallback engine — requests that cannot be satisfied by pinned model/region will be rejected immediately.
- Monitoring: emit a new metric tenant.<tenant>.pin_reject_count with alerting window.

Lead times: we can flip the tenant flags same-day for testing, but guaranteeing steady-state capacity requires a Dedicated pool; procurement for Dedicated typically takes 3–5 business days to provision if hardware is available. For an initial safety net we can enable strict rate limits and configure an alert runbook.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime

Attachments referenced: none

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Prod request — strict region pin + no fallback for PCI workloads

Alan, Priyom — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short product enforcement note below (will convert to a PDF for your security team).

Enforcement summary:
- Policy layer: per-tenant routing policy flags (region_pin: us-east-1, fallback_allowed: false) applied at the API gateway.
- Model pinning: tenant maps to a single model version ID; model variants are excluded for the tenant.
- Runtime behavior: if no capacity in the pinned region/model, requests receive a deterministic 503 with JSON body {"error":"region_pinned_capacity_exhausted"} — we recommend using a dedicated pool to avoid this path.
- Auditability: every routed request will include headers X-tenant-pin, X-routing-decision, and be recorded in the request trace retained for 90 days (longer with enterprise retention).

Recommended contract language for the MAP: Redwood will provide region-pinned serving for AltiCloud PCI workload, with Dedicated capacity sizing TBD and an initial 30-day trial. If Dedicated is not provisioned, Redwood will enable region pin + disable fallback and accept responsibility for 503 behavior under capacity constraints.

I'll prepare a short PDF and a sample routing-policy JSON you can share with your security team.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
PM, Product — Routing & Policy
